sections.title: The Majesty of God
observations: In this brief chapter, Bildad the Shuhite speaks again, emphasizing the greatness and majesty of God. He asserts that God is sovereign and that His power is unmatched. This reflects the common belief among the friends of Job that God is all-powerful and that His justice is absolute.

sections.title: The Human Condition
observations: Bildad poses a rhetorical question about how man can be righteous before God. This highlights the belief that human beings are inherently sinful and cannot stand before a holy God. It serves to remind Job of his own limitations and the need for humility in the face of divine authority.

sections.title: The Unworthiness of Humanity
observations: The chapter concludes with a stark reminder of the frailty of humanity. Bildad compares humans to maggots and worms, emphasizing the idea that in the grand scheme of creation, humans are insignificant. This serves to reinforce the theme of God's transcendence and the lowly state of mankind.

importantVerses.commentary: How can a mortal be righteous before God? This verse encapsulates the central theme of human unworthiness and the need for divine grace.

questions: What does Bildad's speech reveal about the understanding of God's justice among Job's friends?
How does the imagery of humans as maggots and worms affect our understanding of human dignity in relation to God?
In what ways does this chapter challenge our perceptions of righteousness before God?
